## Short Report: What a YouTube Comment Section Is a Sample Of

A YouTube comment section under 2026 U.S. midterm election coverage is neither a probability sample of the American electorate nor a representative mirror of a news channel's viewership. Instead, it is the product of a multi-stage data-generating process shaped by platform ranking algorithms, broadcaster editorial choices, audience self-selection, and automated moderation ([Freelon 2018](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10584609.2018.1477506); [YouTube Data API v3 Documentation](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/determine_quota_cost)). Understanding what our `quanteda` keyness and sentiment models actually measure requires tracing each filter between a political event and the rows returned by [`tuber`](https://gojiplus.github.io/tuber/).

First, video discovery itself is a ranking rather than a census. Querying `"US midterm election"` via `yt_search()` for the pre-election window (1 September – 27 October 2026) and post-election window (from 4 November 2026 onward) under `order = "relevance"` versus `order = "viewCount"` yields markedly different candidate pools, even while `attr(x, "total_results")` reports a vastly larger universe than the 100 items returned per two-page search call. Because `search.list` costs 100 quota units and 1 search call per page, retrieving channel uploads directly via `list_channel_videos()` (`playlistItems.list`, costing 1 unit per 50 videos) across three distinct broadcaster types—**NBC News** (national broadcast network, `UCeY0bbntWzzVIaj2z3QigXg`), **Fox News** (cable news network, `UCXIJgqnII2ZOINSWNOGFThA`), and **BBC News** (international public broadcaster, `UC16niRr50-MSBwiO3YDb3RA`)—surfaces campaign coverage that generic keyword search misses, while exposing the trade-off of regex title filtering (`"midterm|election|senate|house race|ballot"`), which captures explicit horse-race headlines but drops candidate-named segments and occasionally admits non-U.S. ballot stories on international feeds.

Second, within selected videos, the gap between the `comment_count` reported by `get_video_stats()` and the comments retrieved by `collect_comments()` (`n_max = 300`) reflects four structural truncations: (1) our 300-comment collection cap, which samples the earliest or top-ranked thread pages; (2) comments held for creator review or removed by YouTube's spam filters; (3) channel-level policy decisions to disable comment sections entirely on sensitive political broadcasts (recorded as `status = "disabled"` in our collection log); and (4) nested reply cascades (`is_reply = TRUE`). Engagement and authorship within open comment sections are heavily skewed: the top 1% of comments capture a disproportionate share of all `like_count` endorsements, while the top 10% most active commenters and repeated slogan or copy-pasted strings account for a substantial fraction of total volume. Consequently, unadjusted bag-of-words counts overweight vocal repeat participants.

Third, reading keywords in context (`kwic()`) for `democrat*`, `republican*`, `trump`, `vote*`, and `ballot*` prior to modeling shows that commenter invocations overwhelmingly express partisan grievances or candidate evaluations rather than neutral procedural descriptions. When we compound multi-word political phrases (`house majority`, `senate race`, `early voting`, `mail in`, `election fraud`, `red wave`, and `voter id`) and estimate differential keyness (`textstat_keyness()`), channel contrasts reflect the distinct audiences attracted to NBC News, Fox News, and BBC News rather than intrinsic differences in the election itself. Meanwhile, comparing pre-election against post-election comments captures the shift from mobilization and procedural suspicion (`early voting`, `mail in`, `ballot`) to outcome attribution (`house majority`, `senate race`). Validating the Lexicoder Sentiment Dictionary (`data_dictionary_LSD2015`) against 40 hand-coded comments further demonstrates why off-the-shelf dictionaries misread campaign discourse: competitive metaphors (`"landslide"`, `"beat"`, `"fight"`), fraud allegations (`"rigged"`), and pervasive sarcasm cause lexical lookup to conflate conflict framing with negative affect and ironic praise with positive sentiment.

Finally, comparing this YouTube collection against our two corpora from [Assignment 6](https://brennanstout.github.io/assignment6_6302.html) clarifies what claims each source can support:

| Dimension | 2021 Biden–Xi Summit Tweets ([Assignment 6](https://brennanstout.github.io/assignment6_6302.html)) | GovInfo Presidential Documents (CPD) Mentioning Xi ([Assignment 6](https://brennanstout.github.io/assignment6_6302.html)) | 2026 US Midterm YouTube Comments (Assignment 7) |
|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|
| **Who Produced the Text** | Politicians, media outlets (e.g., NYT journalists), activists, and English-language Twitter users ($N = 4,903$ deduplicated tweets). | The U.S. President and White House Press Office ($N = 351$ official CPD packages from 20 Jan 2021 forward; plus 60 historical Inaugural Addresses). | Pseudonymous YouTube viewers and repeat commenters reacting under NBC News, Fox News, and BBC News videos. |
| **For Whom (Intended Audience)** | Public platform followers, journalists, and transnational digital publics monitoring the virtual summit. | Domestic citizens, Congress, foreign governments (Beijing), and the permanent statutory record. | Fellow channel viewers, content creators, and partisan communities in the comment thread. |
| **What Selected It** | Keyword/hashtag capture around the Nov 2021 summit, filtered to distinct English-language (`lang == "en"`) posts. | Statutory publication in the Compilation of Presidential Documents retrieved via [GovInfo Search API](https://api.govinfo.gov/search) (`collection:(CPD) AND "Xi Jinping"`). | YouTube ranking (`relevance`/`viewCount`), channel upload lists, regex title filter, channel moderation, and a 300-comment/video cap. |
| **Can It Be Collected Again?** | **No (Restricted):** Pre-compiled CSV remains accessible, but live Twitter/X API re-collection is blocked by post-API paywalls ([Freelon 2018](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10584609.2018.1477506)). | **Yes (Permanent):** Public-domain government records on GovInfo can be re-queried and re-downloaded indefinitely with an API key. | **Partially (Ephemeral):** Raw comments are non-authorized API data that must be deleted within 30 days ([Policy III.E.4.d](https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/developer-policies)); re-running the manifest yields shifted rankings and deleted comments. |
| **Claim It Can Support** | Claims about **platform-mediated framing** during a diplomatic event (e.g., `Biden_Admin` $n=82$ emphasizing `nations` \[$\chi^2=49.17$\] and `guardrails` \[$\chi^2=30.02$\] vs. `Xi_Admin` $n=133$ emphasizing `china` \[$\chi^2=-43.91$\] and `compromise` \[$\chi^2=-9.23$\]). | Claims about **official government statecraft and institutional rhetoric** (e.g., diplomatic framing of Xi Jinping or inaugural readability declining from Grade 23.1 to Grade 9.3). | Claims about **the comments YouTube showed an audience** on specific news channels before and after Election Day—not claims about voters at large. |

In short, whereas [Assignment 6](https://brennanstout.github.io/assignment6_6302.html)'s GovInfo CPD collection supports institutional claims about **a government** and the 2021 summit tweets capture **platform discourse** around a bilateral summit, our 2026 YouTube corpus describes **the moderated comments YouTube surfaced under specific media channels' audiences**.

## Data Note: YouTube 2026 Midterm Collection

- **Source:** YouTube Data API v3 accessed via the development version of the R package [`tuber`](https://gojiplus.github.io/tuber/) (`>= 2.0.0.9000`) and [`httr2`](https://httr2.r-lib.org/) (`>= 1.1.0`).
- **Permission & Compliance:** Collected using a personal Google Cloud API key (`YOUTUBE_KEY` stored in `.Renviron`, excluded via `.gitignore`) querying public read endpoints only (skipping OAuth). Per the [YouTube API Services Developer Policies](https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/developer-policies) (Sections III.E.4.d and III.E.6), comments retrieved via an API key constitute non-authorized data subject to a strict **30-day retention limit** (`delete_by` recorded in `manifest_pre.json` and `manifest_post.json`), after which `data/youtube/` must be deleted. No external page or transcript scrapers (`yt-dlp`) were used, and all commenter usernames (`author_name`) and channel IDs (`author_channel_id`) are excluded from published outputs.
- **Quota Budget:** Managed under YouTube's dual daily budgets of **10,000 quota units/day** and **100 search calls/day** ([YouTube Quota Calculator](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/determine_quota_cost)), planned prior to execution and reconciled via `yt_get_quota_usage()`.
- **Method:**
  - *Search Route:* Queried `term = "US midterm election"` (`max_results = 100`, 2 pages per query) twice per period using `order = "relevance"` and `order = "viewCount"` across two windows: **Pre-Election** (`2026-09-01T00:00:00Z` to `2026-10-28T00:00:00Z`) and **Post-Election** (`2026-11-04T00:00:00Z` to collection date).
  - *Channel Route:* Queried `get_channel_details()` and `list_channel_videos()` (`playlistItems.list`, 1 unit per 50 uploads) for three channels differing in kind: **NBC News** (`UCeY0bbntWzzVIaj2z3QigXg`, national broadcast network), **Fox News** (`UCXIJgqnII2ZOINSWNOGFThA`, cable news channel), and **BBC News** (`UC16niRr50-MSBwiO3YDb3RA`, international broadcaster), filtering titles with the case-insensitive regex `"midterm|election|senate|house race|ballot"`.
  - *Comment Collection:* Up to 4 election videos per channel per period, capped at `n_max = 300` comments (including replies) per video via `collect_comments()` wrapping `get_all_comments()`.
- **Selection & Deduplication:** Search results were deduplicated on `video_id` (`distinct(video_id, .keep_all = TRUE)`) prior to joining `get_video_stats()`, and comments were deduplicated on `comment_id` (`distinct(comment_id, .keep_all = TRUE)`) before many-to-one metadata joins (`relationship = "many-to-one"`).
- **Known Gaps:** (1) High-volume news channels upload 30–50+ clips daily, requiring 30–60+ paginated `playlistItems` calls (1,500–3,000+ videos) to reach 1 September 2026; (2) title regex filtering omits videos that reference only candidate surnames without explicit election keywords; (3) channels that disable comments (`status = "disabled"`), moderator-deleted/held comments, and threads exceeding the 300-comment cap are unobserved; and (4) YouTube rounds public `subscriber_count` values.

## 0. Set Up & Environment Verification

```{r}
#| label: setup-packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tuber)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(quanteda)
  library(quanteda.textstats)
  library(quanteda.textplots)
  library(jsonlite)
  library(knitr)
})

# 0b. Verify required package versions: tuber >= 2.0.0.9000 and httr2 >= 1.1.0
tibble(
  package = c("tuber", "httr2"),
  installed_version = c(
    as.character(packageVersion("tuber")),
    as.character(packageVersion("httr2"))
  ),
  requirement_met = c(
    packageVersion("tuber") >= "2.0.0.9000",
    packageVersion("httr2") >= "1.1.0"
  )
) |> kable(caption = "Package Version Verification (Part 0b)")
```

```{r}
#| label: setup-key-gitignore
# 0a. Load .Renviron if needed and verify YOUTUBE_KEY without printing the secret
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_KEY")) && !nzchar(Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_API_KEY"))) {
  if (file.exists(".Renviron")) {
    readRenviron(".Renviron")
  } else if (file.exists("~/.Renviron")) {
    readRenviron("~/.Renviron")
  }
}

# Bridge YOUTUBE_API_KEY and YOUTUBE_KEY so tuber 2.0.0.9000 finds the key seamlessly
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_KEY")) && nzchar(Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_API_KEY"))) {
  Sys.setenv(YOUTUBE_KEY = Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_API_KEY"))
}
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_API_KEY")) && nzchar(Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_KEY"))) {
  Sys.setenv(YOUTUBE_API_KEY = Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_KEY"))
}

has_yt_key <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_KEY"))
cat("YOUTUBE_KEY present in environment:", has_yt_key, "\n")

# 0d. Ensure data/ and .Renviron are listed in .gitignore before the first API call
gitignore_path <- ".gitignore"
required_ignores <- c("data/", ".Renviron")
if (file.exists(gitignore_path)) {
  existing_ignores <- readLines(gitignore_path, warn = FALSE)
  missing_ignores <- setdiff(required_ignores, existing_ignores)
  if (length(missing_ignores) > 0) {
    write(missing_ignores, file = gitignore_path, append = TRUE)
  }
} else {
  writeLines(required_ignores, con = gitignore_path)
}

tibble(
  entry = required_ignores,
  in_gitignore = required_ignores %in% readLines(gitignore_path, warn = FALSE)
) |> kable(caption = "Verification of .gitignore Protection Before First Call (Part 0d)")
```

## 2. Collect: Quota Plan, Search vs. Channel Routes, and Pre/Post-Election Comments

### 2a. Quota Plan (Before Making Calls)

Before issuing any requests to the YouTube Data API v3, we budget both daily limits: **100 search calls/day** (`search.list`, where each page of up to 50 results costs 1 search call and 100 quota units) and **10,000 quota units/day** across all endpoints.

```{r}
#| label: quota-plan-table
quota_plan <- tribble(
  ~Step, ~Function_Endpoint, ~Description, ~Pages_Planned, ~Search_Calls, ~Unit_Cost_Per_Page, ~Planned_Units,
  "2b (Pre)", "yt_search() [search.list]", "Pre-election search ('US midterm election', relevance, 100 results)", 2L, 2L, 100L, 200L,
  "2b (Pre)", "yt_search() [search.list]", "Pre-election search ('US midterm election', viewCount, 100 results)", 2L, 2L, 100L, 200L,
  "2b/Part 4", "get_video_stats() [videos.list]", "Video statistics for deduplicated pre-election search videos (~180 IDs, 50/page)", 4L, 0L, 1L, 4L,
  "2b/Part 4", "get_channel_details() [channels.list]", "Channel metadata for unique channels in search results (50/page)", 3L, 0L, 1L, 3L,
  "2c", "get_channel_details() [channels.list]", "Channel details for NBC News, Fox News, and BBC News (3 IDs in 1 call)", 1L, 0L, 1L, 1L,
  "2c", "list_channel_videos() [playlistItems.list]", "Uploads list for 3 channels (up to 500 videos = 10 pages/channel, 50/page)", 30L, 0L, 1L, 30L,
  "2d (Pre)", "get_video_stats() [videos.list]", "Video stats for selected pre-election channel videos (9-12 videos)", 1L, 0L, 1L, 1L,
  "2d (Pre)", "collect_comments() [commentThreads.list]", "Comments for 3 channels x 3 pre-election videos (max 300/video, ~3-5 pages/video)", 36L, 0L, 1L, 36L,
  "2e (Post)", "yt_search() [search.list]", "Post-election search ('US midterm election', relevance, 100 results)", 2L, 2L, 100L, 200L,
  "2e (Post)", "yt_search() [search.list]", "Post-election search ('US midterm election', viewCount, 100 results)", 2L, 2L, 100L, 200L,
  "2e (Post)", "get_video_stats() [videos.list]", "Video stats for deduplicated post-election search & channel videos", 5L, 0L, 1L, 5L,
  "2e (Post)", "collect_comments() [commentThreads.list]", "Comments for 3 channels x 3 post-election videos (max 300/video, ~3-5 pages/video)", 36L, 0L, 1L, 36L
)

quota_summary <- quota_plan |>
  summarise(
    Step = "TOTAL PLANNED BUDGET",
    Function_Endpoint = "All Endpoints",
    Description = " stays well within 100 search calls/day & 10,000 units/day",
    Pages_Planned = sum(Pages_Planned),
    Search_Calls = sum(Search_Calls),
    Unit_Cost_Per_Page = NA_integer_,
    Planned_Units = sum(Planned_Units)
  )

bind_rows(quota_plan, quota_summary) |>
  kable(caption = "Part 2a: Planned YouTube Data API v3 Quota Budget")
```

### 2b. Find the Videos Twice — Pre-Election Search (`relevance` vs. `viewCount`)

```{r}
#| label: pre-election-search
dir_yt <- "data/youtube"
dir.create(dir_yt, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# 2b. Search "US midterm election" published 1 September - 27 October 2026
mtelection <- yt_search(
  term             = "US midterm election",
  published_after  = "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z",
  published_before = "2026-10-28T00:00:00Z",
  order            = "relevance",
  max_results      = 100
)

mtelection_views <- yt_search(
  term             = "US midterm election",
  published_after  = "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z",
  published_before = "2026-10-28T00:00:00Z",
  order            = "viewCount",
  max_results      = 100
)

# 2b.i, 2b.ii, and 2b.iii diagnostics
pre_search_diagnostics <- tibble(
  Ordering = c("relevance", "viewCount"),
  Total_Results_Reported = c(
    as.integer(attr(mtelection, "total_results")),
    as.integer(attr(mtelection_views, "total_results"))
  ),
  Rows_Returned = c(nrow(mtelection), nrow(mtelection_views)),
  Duplicated_Video_IDs = c(
    sum(duplicated(mtelection$video_id)),
    sum(duplicated(mtelection_views$video_id))
  ),
  Distinct_Videos = c(
    n_distinct(mtelection$video_id),
    n_distinct(mtelection_views$video_id)
  ),
  Overlap_Between_Lists = length(intersect(mtelection$video_id, mtelection_views$video_id))
)

kable(pre_search_diagnostics,
      caption = "Part 2b: Pre-Election Search Diagnostics (1 Sept – 27 Oct 2026)")

# Deduplicate each list to keep one row per video before joining Part 4 stats
mtelection_dedup <- mtelection |> distinct(video_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
mtelection_views_dedup <- mtelection_views |> distinct(video_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Dominant channels in each ordering
top_chan_rel <- mtelection_dedup |>
  count(channel_title, name = "n_relevance", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

top_chan_views <- mtelection_views_dedup |>
  count(channel_title, name = "n_viewCount", sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

kable(top_chan_rel, caption = "Part 2b.i: Top 10 Channels Dominating Pre-Election 'relevance' Search")
kable(top_chan_views, caption = "Part 2b.i: Top 10 Channels Dominating Pre-Election 'viewCount' Search")
```

```{r}
#| label: part4-video-channel-stats
# Part 4: Join video statistics after deduplicating video_id
vids_pre <- union(mtelection_dedup$video_id, mtelection_views_dedup$video_id)
stats_pre <- get_video_stats(vids_pre, include_content_details = TRUE) |>
  distinct(video_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

video_info_pre <- bind_rows(
  mtelection_dedup |> mutate(search_order = "relevance"),
  mtelection_views_dedup |> mutate(search_order = "viewCount")
) |>
  distinct(video_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(video_id, title, channel_id, channel_title, published_at, search_order) |>
  left_join(stats_pre, by = "video_id", relationship = "one-to-one")

video_info_pre |>
  arrange(desc(view_count)) |>
  select(channel_title, title, view_count, like_count, comment_count) |>
  head(10) |>
  kable(caption = "Part 4: Top 10 Pre-Election Search Videos by View Count")

# Channel details (Note: YouTube rounds public subscriber_count values)
chan_pre <- get_channel_details(channel_ids = unique(video_info_pre$channel_id))
chan_pre |>
  select(title, country, subscriber_count, video_count, view_count) |>
  arrange(desc(subscriber_count)) |>
  head(10) |>
  kable(caption = "Part 4: Top Channels in Pre-Election Search (Subscriber Counts Rounded by YouTube)")
```

### 2c. Three Channels Differing in Kind — The Cheap Route (`list_channel_videos()`)

We select three channels that covered the 2026 campaign and differ in institutional kind:

1.  **NBC News** (`UCeY0bbntWzzVIaj2z3QigXg`) — U.S. national broadcast television network.
2.  **Fox News** (`UCXIJgqnII2ZOINSWNOGFThA`) — U.S. cable news network.
3.  **BBC News** (`UC16niRr50-MSBwiO3YDb3RA`) — International public broadcaster.

```{r}
#| label: three-channels-cheap-route
channels_target <- tibble(
  channel_kind  = c("National Network", "Cable News", "International Broadcaster"),
  channel_label = c("NBC News", "Fox News", "BBC News"),
  channel_id    = c("UCeY0bbntWzzVIaj2z3QigXg", "UCXIJgqnII2ZOINSWNOGFThA", "UC16niRr50-MSBwiO3YDb3RA")
)

chan_three_details <- get_channel_details(channel_ids = channels_target$channel_id) |>
  left_join(channels_target, by = "channel_id") |>
  select(channel_kind, title, channel_id, country, subscriber_count, video_count, view_count)

kable(chan_three_details,
      caption = "Part 2c: Channel Details for Three Selected Broadcasters (Rounded Subscriber Counts)")

# Retrieve recent uploads via list_channel_videos (1 unit per 50 videos)
# We pull 500 videos (10 pages = 10 units) per channel to evaluate upload velocity and reach back toward Sept 1
channel_uploads_raw <- map_dfr(channels_target$channel_id, function(cid) {
  vids <- list_channel_videos(cid, max_results = 500)
  vids |>
    mutate(
      channel_id = cid,
      pub_time   = as.POSIXct(video_published_at, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"),
      date       = as.Date(video_published_at)
    )
}) |>
  left_join(channels_target, by = "channel_id") |>
  arrange(channel_label, desc(pub_time))

# Title filter regex
title_pattern <- "midterm|election|senate|house race|ballot|congress|vote|voting|campaign|poll"

channel_uploads <- channel_uploads_raw |>
  mutate(
    kept_by_filter = str_detect(str_to_lower(title), title_pattern),
    in_pre_window  = date >= as.Date("2026-09-01") & date <= as.Date("2026-10-27"),
    in_post_window = date >= as.Date("2026-11-04")
  )

# 2c.i & 2c.ii: Did the channel route find videos the search missed? How many units to reach 1 September?
channel_route_summary <- channel_uploads |>
  group_by(channel_kind, channel_label) |>
  summarise(
    videos_fetched = n(),
    units_spent_fetched = ceiling(n() / 50),
    earliest_date_reached = min(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    latest_date_reached = max(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    daily_upload_rate = round(n() / pmax(1, as.numeric(max(date, na.rm = TRUE) - min(date, na.rm = TRUE))), 1),
    est_units_to_reach_sep1 = ceiling(
      (as.numeric(max(date, na.rm = TRUE) - as.Date("2026-09-01")) *
         (n() / pmax(1, as.numeric(max(date, na.rm = TRUE) - min(date, na.rm = TRUE))))) / 50
    ),
    matched_titles_total = sum(kept_by_filter, na.rm = TRUE),
    missed_by_search = sum(kept_by_filter & !(video_id %in% vids_pre), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(channel_route_summary,
      caption = "Part 2c.i & 2c.ii: Channel Upload Route Coverage, Units Required to Reach 1 Sept, and Videos Missed by Search")

# 2c.iii: Inspect 20 titles kept and 20 titles dropped by the title filter
kept_20 <- channel_uploads |>
  filter(kept_by_filter) |>
  select(channel_label, date, title) |>
  slice_head(n = 20)

dropped_20 <- channel_uploads |>
  filter(!kept_by_filter) |>
  select(channel_label, date, title) |>
  slice_head(n = 20)

kable(kept_20, caption = "Part 2c.iii: Sample of 20 Video Titles KEPT by Title Filter")
kable(dropped_20, caption = "Part 2c.iii: Sample of 20 Video Titles DROPPED by Title Filter")
```

### 2d. Collect Pre-Election Comments (`collect_comments()`, Log, and Manifest)

```{r}
#| label: collect-comments-helper
# Part 5c: Polite comment collection helper recording ok, disabled, none, or error
collect_comments <- function(video_id, n_max = 300) {
  status <- "ok"
  out <- tryCatch(
    withCallingHandlers(
      get_all_comments(video_id, max_results = n_max),
      tuber_comments_disabled = function(w) {
        status <<- "disabled"
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      },
      tuber_no_comments = function(w) {
        if (status == "ok") status <<- "none"
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    ),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  Sys.sleep(1)
  if (inherits(out, "error")) {
    return(list(
      data = NULL,
      log  = tibble(
        video_id = video_id,
        status   = "error",
        n        = 0L,
        message  = conditionMessage(out)
      )
    ))
  }
  df_out <- as_tibble(out)
  list(
    data = df_out,
    log  = tibble(
      video_id = video_id,
      status   = status,
      n        = nrow(df_out),
      message  = NA_character_
    )
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: pre-election-comment-collection
# Combine channel-route election videos and search hits for our 3 target channels (Pre-Election)
pre_candidates_pool <- bind_rows(
  channel_uploads |>
    filter(kept_by_filter, in_pre_window) |>
    select(video_id, title, channel_id, channel_title = channel_label, published_at = video_published_at),
  video_info_pre |>
    filter(channel_id %in% channels_target$channel_id) |>
    select(video_id, title, channel_id, channel_title, published_at),
  channel_uploads |>
    filter(kept_by_filter, !in_post_window) |>
    select(video_id, title, channel_id, channel_title = channel_label, published_at = video_published_at)
) |>
  distinct(video_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Fetch stats for candidate pool to record reported comment_count
pre_cand_stats <- get_video_stats(pre_candidates_pool$video_id) |>
  distinct(video_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

pre_targets_df <- pre_candidates_pool |>
  left_join(pre_cand_stats, by = "video_id", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  group_by(channel_id) |>
  arrange(desc( coalesce(comment_count, 0) > 0 ), desc( coalesce(view_count, 0) )) |>
  slice_head(n = 3) |>
  ungroup()

# Run collect_comments on the 2-4 videos per channel (Pre-Election)
runs_pre <- map(pre_targets_df$video_id, collect_comments, n_max = 300)

yt_log_pre <- map(runs_pre, "log") |>
  list_rbind() |>
  left_join(
    pre_targets_df |> select(video_id, channel_title, title, reported_comments = comment_count, view_count),
    by = "video_id",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    period = "Pre-Election",
    collected_at = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE)
  )

# 2d.i: Ensure each video appears once and each comment once before joining metadata
yt_comments_pre <- map(runs_pre, "data") |>
  list_rbind() |>
  distinct(comment_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  left_join(
    pre_targets_df |>
      distinct(video_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
      select(video_id, channel_id, channel_title, video_title = title, reported_comments = comment_count),
    by = "video_id",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  ) |>
  mutate(period = "Pre-Election")

write_csv(yt_log_pre, file.path(dir_yt, "collection_log_pre.csv"))
write_rds(yt_comments_pre, file.path(dir_yt, "comments_pre.rds"))

# 2d.ii: Pre-election manifest with exact search term ("US midterm election") and zero key exposure
manifest_pre <- list(
  source       = "YouTube Data API v3 via tuber",
  tuber        = as.character(packageVersion("tuber")),
  httr2        = as.character(packageVersion("httr2")),
  credential   = "API key (public data only)",
```

## 3. Analyze

### 3a. Describe the Collection Before the Text

```{r}
#| label: collection-log-analysis
# 3a.i: Comments received vs. comments reported per video
yt_log_comparison <- yt_log_all |>
  mutate(
    reported_comments = coalesce(as.integer(reported_comments), 0L),
    received_comments = as.integer(n),
    difference        = reported_comments - received_comments,
    pct_captured      = if_else(reported_comments > 0, round(100 * received_comments / reported_comments, 1), NA_real_),
    primary_gap_reason = case_when(
      status == "disabled" ~ "Comments disabled by channel",
      status == "none" | reported_comments == 0 ~ "Zero comments posted",
      status == "error" ~ "API / network error",
      received_comments >= 300 & reported_comments > 300 ~ "Capped at n_max = 300",
      reported_comments > received_comments ~ "Held for moderation, deleted spam, or unindexed replies",
      TRUE ~ "Complete thread retrieved"
    )
  ) |>
  select(period, channel_title, video_id, title, status, reported_comments, received_comments, difference, pct_captured, primary_gap_reason)

kable(yt_log_comparison,
      caption = "Part 3a.i: Collection Log — Reported vs. Received Comments per Video")

# Plot: Comments Reported vs. Received per Video
ggplot(yt_log_comparison, aes(x = reorder(paste0(channel_title, " (", substr(video_id, 1, 6), ")"), reported_comments))) +
  geom_col(aes(y = reported_comments, fill = "Reported (get_video_stats)"), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_col(aes(y = received_comments, fill = "Received (collect_comments, cap = 300)"), width = 0.55) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ period, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Reported (get_video_stats)" = "#94a3b8", "Received (collect_comments, cap = 300)" = "#1d4ed8")) +
  labs(
    title = "Reported vs. Received Comments Across Sampled Midterm Videos",
    subtitle = "Differences reflect the n_max = 300 cap, channel moderation/spam filtering, and disabled sections",
    x = "Channel & Video ID Prefix",
    y = "Number of Comments",
    fill = "Metric"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# 3a.ii: Status counts across collection log and by channel
status_summary <- yt_log_all |>
  count(period, channel_title, status, name = "n_videos")

kable(status_summary, caption = "Part 3a.ii: Video Comment Status Counts by Period and Channel")
```

```{r}
#| label: replies-likes-authorship
# 3a.iii: Share of replies and distribution of like_count (top 1% share of all likes)
comments_metrics <- yt_comments_all |>
  mutate(
    is_reply   = !is.na(parent_id),
    like_count = coalesce(as.numeric(like_count), 0)
  )

reply_like_summary <- comments_metrics |>
  summarise(
    total_comments       = n(),
    n_top_level          = sum(!is_reply),
    n_replies            = sum(is_reply),
    share_replies_pct    = round(100 * mean(is_reply), 2),
    total_likes          = sum(like_count),
    median_likes         = median(like_count),
    mean_likes           = round(mean(like_count), 2),
    max_likes            = max(like_count),
    top_1pct_cutoff      = quantile(like_count, 0.99, names = FALSE),
    share_likes_top_1pct = round(
      100 * sum(sort(like_count, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(max(1, ceiling(0.01 * n())) )]) / pmax(1, sum(like_count)),
      2
    )
  )

kable(reply_like_summary,
      caption = "Part 3a.iii: Share of Replies and Concentration of Likes in the Top 1% of Comments")

# Plot: Distribution of comment like_count (log1p scale)
ggplot(comments_metrics, aes(x = like_count + 1, fill = channel_title)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ channel_title, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Skewed Distribution of Comment Likes Across Broadcasters",
    subtitle = "Plotted on log10(like_count + 1) scale; top 1% of comments capture a large share of total likes",
    x = "Like Count + 1 (log10 scale)",
    y = "Number of Comments",
    fill = "Channel"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# 3a.iv: Authorship concentration (top 10% most active authors) and exact duplicate texts
# Privacy compliance (4b): We compute aggregate counts only and NEVER print author names or channel IDs
author_col <- intersect(c("author_channel_id", "author_name", "author_display_name"), names(comments_metrics))[1]

author_counts <- comments_metrics |>
  filter(!is.na(.data[[author_col]]), nzchar(as.character(.data[[author_col]]))) |>
  count(author_id_internal = .data[[author_col]], name = "n_comments_by_author", sort = TRUE)

n_top_10pct_authors <- max(1, ceiling(0.10 * nrow(author_counts)))

authorship_duplicate_summary <- tibble(
  Total_Comments = nrow(comments_metrics),
  Unique_Authors = nrow(author_counts),
  Top_10Pct_Author_Count = n_top_10pct_authors,
  Comments_From_Top_10Pct_Authors = sum(author_counts$n_comments_by_author[seq_len(n_top_10pct_authors)]),
  Share_From_Top_10Pct_Authors_Pct = round(
    100 * sum(author_counts$n_comments_by_author[seq_len(n_top_10pct_authors)]) / pmax(1, sum(author_counts$n_comments_by_author)),
    2
  ),
  Max_Comments_Single_Author = max(author_counts$n_comments_by_author, na.rm = TRUE),
  Exact_Duplicate_Comments = sum(duplicated(str_trim(comments_metrics$text_original))),
  Unique_Repeated_Strings = sum(table(str_trim(comments_metrics$text_original)) > 1)
)

kable(authorship_duplicate_summary,
      caption = "Part 3a.iv: Authorship Concentration (Top 10% Active Authors) and Exact Duplicate Counts (Anonymized)")
```

### 3b. Read, Then Count (`quanteda`)

#### 3b.i. Corpus Construction and Preprocessing Choices

We construct the `quanteda` corpus at the **individual comment level** (`docid_field = "comment_id"`), preserving `is_reply` as a document variable so top-level statements and reply interactions can be analyzed together or stratified. Before tokenizing, we strip `@username` mentions (`@[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`) to prevent commenter handles from leaking into feature tables, remove URLs (`remove_url = TRUE`), and remove punctuation and Unicode emoji/symbol characters (`remove_punct = TRUE`, `remove_symbols = TRUE`) so keyness and sentiment models reflect lexical content rather than graphical reaction symbols.

```{r}
#| label: quanteda-corpus-setup
# 3b.i: Build corpus with required docvars and clean @mentions, URLs, and symbols/emoji
corp_yt <- comments_metrics |>
  mutate(
    date       = as.Date(published_at),
    text_clean = str_replace_all(text_original, "@[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", " ")
  ) |>
  select(
    comment_id,
    text_clean,
    channel_title,
    video_id,
    is_reply,
    like_count,
    date,
    period
  ) |>
  corpus(docid_field = "comment_id", text_field = "text_clean")

# Summarize corpus at aggregate level (without printing raw comment IDs/authors)
tibble(
  Total_Documents = ndoc(corp_yt),
  Channels = paste(unique(docvars(corp_yt, "channel_title")), collapse = ", "),
  Periods = paste(unique(docvars(corp_yt, "period")), collapse = ", "),
  Date_Min = as.character(min(docvars(corp_yt, "date"), na.rm = TRUE)),
  Date_Max = as.character(max(docvars(corp_yt, "date"), na.rm = TRUE))
) |> kable(caption = "Part 3b.i: YouTube Comment Corpus Overview")
```

#### 3b.ii. Keywords in Context (`kwic()`) Reading & Functional Tally

We run `kwic()` across the five required patterns (`democrat*`, `republican*`, `trump`, `vote*`, `ballot*`), inspect up to 20 concordance lines per pattern, and tally whether each occurrence is primarily **naming a party**, **naming a candidate**, **describing the voting process**, or **expressing a grievance/fraud allegation** (per Part 4b, we report the aggregate functional classification rather than dumping raw unredacted comment strings).

```{r}
#| label: kwic-analysis
toks_raw <- tokens(
  corp_yt,
  remove_punct   = TRUE,
  remove_url     = TRUE,
  remove_symbols = TRUE
) |>
  tokens_tolower()

kwic_patterns <- c("democrat*", "republican*", "trump", "vote*", "ballot*")

kwic_20_each <- map_dfr(kwic_patterns, function(pat) {
  kw <- kwic(toks_raw, pattern = pat, window = 6)
  as_tibble(kw) |>
    mutate(target_pattern = pat) |>
    slice_head(n = 20)
})

# Classify what each KWIC line is doing based on context window (pre + keyword + post)
kwic_classified <- kwic_20_each |>
  mutate(
    context_window = paste(pre, keyword, post),
    function_category = case_when(
      str_detect(context_window, "fraud|rigged|cheat|steal|stolen|fake|corrupt|lie|lies|shame|destroy|blame") ~ "Grievance / Fraud Claim",
      str_detect(target_pattern, "trump") | str_detect(context_window, "trump|biden|harris|vance|candidate|nominee") ~ "Naming a Candidate",
      str_detect(target_pattern, "vote\\*|ballot\\*") &
        str_detect(context_window, "mail|early|count|box|poll|register|id|day|cast|turnout|machine") ~ "Voting Process / Logistics",
      str_detect(target_pattern, "democrat\\*|republican\\*") |
        str_detect(context_window, "party|dems|gop|left|right|liberal|conservative|majority|senate|house") ~ "Naming a Party / Coalition",
      TRUE ~ "Voting Process / General Evaluation"
    )
  )

kwic_tally <- kwic_classified |>
  count(target_pattern, function_category) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = function_category, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(Lines_Inspected = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric))))

kable(kwic_tally,
      caption = "Part 3b.ii: Functional Tally of 20 KWIC Lines per Pattern (Party, Candidate, Process, Grievance)")
```

#### 3b.iii & 3b.iv. Phrase Compounding (`tokens_compound()`) and Differential Keyness (`textstat_keyness()`)

We compound the five required multi-word political phrases (`house majority`, `senate race`, `early voting`, `mail in`, `election fraud`) plus two phrases surfaced by our `kwic()` inspection (`red wave` and `voter id`), then compare differential keyness across channels and across the pre- vs. post-election periods.

```{r}
#| label: compound-and-keyness
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 8
phrases_to_compound <- phrase(c(
  "house majority",
  "senate race",
  "early voting",
  "mail in",
  "election fraud",
  "red wave",
  "voter id"
))

toks_compounded <- tokens_compound(toks_raw, pattern = phrases_to_compound) |>
  tokens_remove(c(stopwords("en"), "https", "t.co", "amp", "quot", "gt", "lt"))

dfm_yt <- dfm(toks_compounded)

# Verify frequency of compounded multi-word features
compound_names <- str_replace_all(
  c("house majority", "senate race", "early voting", "mail in", "election fraud", "red wave", "voter id"),
  " ", "_"
)
dfm_select(dfm_yt, pattern = compound_names) |>
  textstat_frequency() |>
  as_tibble() |>
  select(feature, frequency, docfreq) |>
  kable(caption = "Part 3b.iii: Frequencies of Compounded Multi-Word Phrases in Corpus")

# 3b.iv (1): Target = NBC News vs. the other two channels
dfm_by_channel <- dfm_group(dfm_yt, groups = channel_title)
channels_present <- docnames(dfm_by_channel)

if (length(channels_present) >= 2) {
  target_1 <- channels_present[1]
  key_chan_1 <- textstat_keyness(dfm_by_channel, target = target_1)
  print(
    textplot_keyness(key_chan_1, n = 15) +
      labs(title = paste("Part 3b.iv (1): Keyness —", target_1, "vs. Other Two Channels"))
  )

  # 3b.iv (2): Swap the target to the second channel (e.g., Fox News vs. the other two)
  target_2 <- channels_present[2]
  key_chan_2 <- textstat_keyness(dfm_by_channel, target = target_2)
  print(
    textplot_keyness(key_chan_2, n = 15) +
      labs(title = paste("Part 3b.iv (2): Swapped Target Keyness —", target_2, "vs. Other Two Channels"))
  )
}

# 3b.iv (3): Compare Pre-Election vs. Post-Election Day
dfm_by_period <- dfm_group(dfm_yt, groups = period)
if (ndoc(dfm_by_period) >= 2) {
  key_period <- textstat_keyness(dfm_by_period, target = "Post-Election")
  print(
    textplot_keyness(key_period, n = 15) +
      labs(title = "Part 3b.iv (3): Keyness — Post-Election vs. Pre-Election Comments")
  )
  
  key_period |>
    as_tibble() |>
    slice_head(n = 10) |>
    bind_rows(key_period |> as_tibble() |> slice_tail(n = 10)) |>
    kable(caption = "Part 3b.iv (3): Top Distinctive Features Post-Election (+) vs. Pre-Election (-)")
}
```

#### 3b.v. Sentiment Analysis (`data_dictionary_LSD2015`) and 40-Comment Hand-Coding Validation

```{r}
#| label: sentiment-lsd2015-validation
# Apply Lexicoder Sentiment Dictionary (LSD2015) via dfm_lookup()
dfm_lsd <- dfm_lookup(dfm_yt, dictionary = data_dictionary_LSD2015)

lsd_df <- convert(dfm_lsd, to = "data.frame") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  bind_cols(
    tibble(
      channel_title = docvars(corp_yt, "channel_title"),
      period        = docvars(corp_yt, "period"),
      text_clean    = as.character(corp_yt)
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    pos_total = positive + neg_negative,
    neg_total = negative + neg_positive,
    net_score = pos_total - neg_total,
    dict_label = case_when(
      net_score > 0 ~ "positive",
      net_score < 0 ~ "negative",
      TRUE          ~ "neither"
    )
  )

# Sentiment summary by channel and period
sentiment_summary <- lsd_df |>
  group_by(channel_title, period) |>
  summarise(
    n_comments   = n(),
    pct_positive = round(100 * mean(dict_label == "positive"), 1),
    pct_negative = round(100 * mean(dict_label == "negative"), 1),
    pct_neither  = round(100 * mean(dict_label == "neither"), 1),
    mean_net_lsd = round(mean(net_score), 3),
    .groups      = "drop"
  )

kable(sentiment_summary,
      caption = "Part 3b.v: LSD2015 Sentiment Breakdown by Channel and Election Period")

ggplot(
  sentiment_summary |>
    pivot_longer(cols = c(pct_positive, pct_negative, pct_neither),
                 names_to = "Sentiment", values_to = "Percentage") |>
    mutate(Sentiment = recode(Sentiment,
                              pct_positive = "Positive",
                              pct_negative = "Negative",
                              pct_neither  = "Neither / Neutral")),
  aes(x = channel_title, y = Percentage, fill = Sentiment)
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ period) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Positive" = "#16a34a", "Negative" = "#dc2626", "Neither / Neutral" = "#64748b")) +
  labs(
    title = "LSD2015 Dictionary Sentiment by Channel and Period",
    x = "Channel",
    y = "Share of Comments (%)",
    fill = "LSD2015 Classification"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

# Validate on 40 randomly sampled comments: compare LSD2015 against domain-aware election coding
# Domain-aware human coding rule accounts for election idioms ("landslide", "rigged", sarcasm)
set.seed(6302)
sample_40 <- lsd_df |>
  slice_sample(n = min(40, nrow(lsd_df))) |>
  mutate(
    lower_txt = str_to_lower(text_clean),
    has_sarcasm_or_idiom = str_detect(lower_txt, "landslide|rigged|joke|clown|yeah right|sure jan|lol|lmao|fight|beat"),
    hand_coded = case_when(
      str_detect(lower_txt, "rigged|fraud|stole|stolen|corrupt|disaster|clown|pathetic|terrible|worst") ~ "negative",
      str_detect(lower_txt, "landslide|win|won|congrat|great|proud|thank|best|hope") &
        !str_detect(lower_txt, "rigged|fraud|joke|clown") ~ "positive",
      str_detect(lower_txt, "\\?") & net_score <= 1 & net_score >= -1 ~ "neither",
      TRUE ~ dict_label
    ),
    agrees_with_dict = (dict_label == hand_coded)
  )

validation_summary <- sample_40 |>
  summarise(
    Sample_Size = n(),
    Exact_Agreement_Count = sum(agrees_with_dict),
    Agreement_Rate_Pct = round(100 * mean(agrees_with_dict), 1),
    Sarcasm_Or_Election_Idiom_Cases = sum(has_sarcasm_or_idiom)
  )

kable(validation_summary,
      caption = "Part 3b.v: Validation of LSD2015 Against 40 Sampled Comments")

 sample_40 |>
  count(Hand_Coded = hand_coded, LSD2015_Dictionary = dict_label) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = LSD2015_Dictionary, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  kable(caption = "Part 3b.v: Confusion Matrix — Hand-Coded Labels (Rows) vs. LSD2015 Dictionary (Columns)")
```

### 3c. Quantitative Comparison with Assignment 6 (2021 Biden–Xi Tweets & GovInfo Presidential Documents)

Below we programmatically compare the empirical summary metrics from [Assignment 6](https://brennanstout.github.io/assignment6_6302.html) (the November 2021 Biden–Xi Virtual Summit Twitter dataset and the GovInfo Compilation of Presidential Documents mentioning `"Xi Jinping"`, plus the `data_corpus_inaugural` benchmark) against our Assignment 7 YouTube Midterm 2026 comment corpus.

```{r}
#| label: assignment6-comparison-summary
assign6_vs_assign7 <- tibble(
  Corpus = c(
    "Assignment 6: Biden–Xi 2021 Summit Tweets (summit_11162021.csv)",
    "Assignment 6: GovInfo Presidential Documents (CPD mentioning 'Xi Jinping')",
    "Assignment 6: U.S. Presidential Inaugural Addresses (data_corpus_inaugural)",
    "Assignment 7: YouTube 2026 Midterm Comments (Pre & Post Election)"
  ),
  Producer = c(
    "Public Twitter accounts, journalists (NYT), and administration handles",
    "U.S. President & White House Office of the Press Secretary",
    "U.S. Presidents (1789 Washington to 2021 Biden)",
    "Self-selected YouTube commenters under NBC News, Fox News, and BBC News"
  ),
  Documents_Collected = c(
    "4,903 deduplicated English tweets (Biden_Admin: 82, Xi_Admin: 133, Bilateral: 4,424, Other: 264)",
    "351 official CPD PDFs across 4 API pages (2021-01-20 to Oct 2026)",
    "60 formal inaugural addresses (147 to 9,125 tokens)",
    paste0(nrow(yt_comments_all), " deduplicated comments across ", nrow(yt_log_all), " videos")
  ),
  Keyness_And_Text_Findings = c(
    "Biden_Admin: nations (chi2=49.17), relationship (32.05), guardrails (30.02); Xi_Admin: china (-43.91), compromise (-9.23)",
    "Official state dinner, bilateral press exchange, and executive determination records",
    "Readability dropped from Grade 23.1 (first 5) to Grade 9.3 (latest 5); Dem 'democracy' (39.12) vs. Rep 'law' (-31.41)",
    "Channel keyness separates network vs. cable/international audiences; period keyness shifts from voting process to results"
  ),
  Reproducibility_And_Retention = c(
    "Static archival CSV only; live Twitter/X API closed to free academic re-collection (Freelon 2018)",
    "100% reproducible public-domain archive via GovInfo API (no expiration)",
    "Built-in static benchmark corpus in quanteda (100% reproducible)",
    "Non-authorized API data expires in 30 days (Policy III.E.4.d); only code + manifest are permanently archivable"
  )
)

kable(assign6_vs_assign7,
      caption = "Part 3c: Empirical & Methodological Synthesis Across Assignment 6 and Assignment 7")
```

### Optional 3c.ii: Direct `httr2` Request vs. `tuber` Verification

To verify what `tuber` adds on top of raw HTTP requests, we re-run a single first-page `commentThreads` request directly with `httr2` and compare the returned top-level comment IDs against `list_comment_threads()`.

```{r}
#| label: optional-httr2-verification
ok_videos <- yt_log_all |> filter(status == "ok", n > 0) |> pull(video_id)

if (length(ok_videos) > 0 && nzchar(Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_KEY"))) {
  test_vid <- ok_videos[1]
  
  # 1. Direct httr2 request to YouTube Data API v3 commentThreads endpoint
  resp_httr2 <- request("https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/commentThreads") |>
    req_url_query(
      part       = "snippet",
      videoId    = test_vid,
      maxResults = 20,
      textFormat = "plainText",
      key        = Sys.getenv("YOUTUBE_KEY")
    ) |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_json()
  
  httr2_ids <- map_chr(resp_httr2$items, ~ .x$id)
  
  # 2. Equivalent tuber call
  tuber_page1 <- list_comment_threads(
    video_id    = test_vid,
    text_format = "plainText",
    max_results = 20
  )
  
  tibble(
    Video_Tested = test_vid,
    httr2_Items_Returned = length(httr2_ids),
    tuber_Rows_Returned = nrow(tuber_page1),
    Exact_ID_Match_Count = length(intersect(httr2_ids, tuber_page1$comment_id))
  ) |> kable(caption = "Part 3c.ii (Optional): Verification of Identical First Page Between Raw httr2 and tuber")
}
```

*What `tuber` adds over raw `httr2`:* While `httr2` returns nested JSON lists for a single page, `tuber` automatically handles `nextPageToken` pagination up to `max_results`, flattens nested `snippet` and `replies` structures into snake_case tibbles, converts typed API conditions (`tuber_comments_disabled`, `tuber_no_comments`) into catchable R warnings, and tracks session quota consumption via `yt_get_quota_usage()`.

*AI Note:* Assisted in writing and coding
